sources.name: Study in Korea Living and Housing Guide
factual_notes: The government guide identifies dormitories and private housing as common international-student options.
It distinguishes wolse, with a deposit and recurring monthly rent, from jeonse, with a large lump-sum deposit and no monthly rent.
It advises visiting a property in person before signing rather than relying only on online information.
It points students to real-estate applications as search tools, which the article treats only as listing leads rather than verification.

sources.name: Easy Law Finding a Home for International Students
factual_notes: The guide compares dormitories, boarding houses, and wolse or jeonse housing by cost structure, convenience, privacy, and rules.
It advises checking real-estate registration records for ownership, mortgages, lease rights, and other interests before contracting.
It explains that residence reporting and a fixed date are relevant to deposit priority protection.
It states current lease-reporting thresholds and a 30-day reporting period for covered contracts and jurisdictions.
It notes Seoul's designated global real-estate offices for foreign-language lease guidance.

sources.name: Easy Law English Lease Agreements Guide
factual_notes: The English guide explains application of the Housing Lease Protection Act to foreign nationals.
It says a foreign tenant who completes alien registration and reports a change of residence may exceptionally receive protection under the Act.
The article therefore directs readers to verify their own protection steps with the responsible local office.

sources.name: MOLIT Real Estate Transaction Management System
factual_notes: The Ministry of Land system supports online housing-lease reporting and issuance of a reporting certificate.
Its system overview explains that a contract copy can support a report by one party under the described electronic process.
The article links readers to the official system but tells them to confirm coverage and current procedure for the exact contract.

sources.name: Korea Immigration Service Customized Stay Guide
factual_notes: Registered foreign residents must report a change of residence within 15 days, while F-4 holders have a 14-day period in the guide.
The listed documents are passport, residence card, application form, and proof of residence.
The guide says applications can be filed online through Hi Korea.

sources.name: Korea Immigration Contact Center 1345
factual_notes: The Ministry of Justice contact center provides counseling on immigration and living in Korea.
It offers multilingual support and can be reached by dialing 1345 in Korea.
The article recommends it when proof-of-residence or reporting requirements are unclear.

sources.name: Yonsei University 2026 Spring Housing Notice
factual_notes: Exchange and visiting students were eligible for the cited semester, but housing was not guaranteed and assignments were first come, first served.
The notice separates application, result, payment, housing-period, and refund deadlines.
It lists wire transfer, Wise, and Flywire as semester-specific payment methods.
Missing the payment deadline could cancel housing without notice, and the notice provides a full-refund cutoff before move-in.
The article frames all dates, prices, and methods as one university example rather than a national rule.

sources.name: Seoul Foreign Resident Center Safe Jeonse and Wolse Seminar
factual_notes: The Seoul Foreign Resident Center's program organized lease safety into checks before signing, during contracting, and after signing.
Its published scope included identifying a bad house, checking monthly rent, verifying a broker, writing the contract, and required post-contract reports.
The article uses this as support for the same three-stage safety structure without relying on expired event registration information.
